paragraphs: Bytecurve sells operations software for school bus fleets, tying routing and GPS data into driver management, dispatching and payroll. The company pitches its payroll application as one that catches pay inconsistencies, and says it was built by people who worked in K12 transportation. Private student transportation contractors are one audience for it, and school districts are the other.

Real-time integration with routing systems and GPS lets dispatchers reassign drivers on the fly and break routes apart. Time and attendance removes manual calculation of employee guarantees, contracts and overtime, and runs through a mobile app or a garage-based tablet. Drivers check in and out remotely, view schedules and receive messages on their phones. Dispatchers get immediate alerts for late or missing drivers, and access to the driver app is limited to authorized employees through a customer-specific code.

The company says dozens of districts use the system across more than 40,000 buses and 50,000 drivers. Its founders claim over 30 years of combined transportation experience, with a focus on student transportation. One case study states that Rome Public Schools reduced payroll by $30,000 per month.
